## Variants of Betweenness


### Standard Betweenness Centrality

**What is betweenness centrality?**
\
The sum of probabilities of passing through a given node on the shortest path between two others. 

**What it describes in the network:**
\
Betweenness highlights individuals who facilitate direct and indirect interactions between nodes. It captures a quality of bridging two nodes, but not necessarily bridging between two clusters or political factions, in our case. 

**Why does this fall short when considering our research questions?**
\
Betweenness needs to be modified to capture the moderating behavior between Government and Opposition. It's also not a direct indication of local bridging behavior, really more of a global view. Standard betweenness doesn't take weights into account; also assumes shortest paths are the relevant paths. 

**Formula:**
 $$
C_B(v) = \sum_{s \neq v \neq t}\frac{\sigma_{st}(v)}{\sigma_{st}}$$



Where:
\
- $\sigma_{st}$: Total number of shortest paths from node $s$ to node $t$.
\
- $\sigma_{st}(v)$: Number of shortest paths from node $s$ to $t$ that pass through $v$.

### Candidate Variant #1 - Cross-Betweenness

**What are we altering?**
\
Instead of considering the shortest path between every pair of nodes, we only use distinct pairs of nodes with opposing affiliation (Government and Opposition). 

Here we only evaluate the ability of a node to bridge the gap between the factions. 

We ignore connectivity within each faction, since this is not relevant to our research.

**Formula:**
 $$
C_B(v) = \sum_{o \neq v \neq g}\frac{\sigma_{og}(v)}{\sigma_{og}}$$

Where:
\
- $\sigma_{og}$: Total number of shortest paths from node $o$, an opposition node, to node $g$, a government node.
\
- $\sigma_{og}(v)$: Number of shortest paths from node $o$ to $g$ that pass through $v$.

**Concerns / Potential Pitfalls:**
\
Large, dense clusters can skew the centrality, inflating the scores of nodes because they lie on multiple paths within the same cluster. This could mask who is genuinely "important" as a moderator.
\
Perhaps indirect interactions are not as important as direct interactions, in which case the global nature of this method doesn't help us in our research. 

#### Exploring this Variant (Cross-Betweenness)

Below we'll share a glimpse at the top 20 highest cross-betweenness results. The results are currently calculated for a single year. This is only because our function needs to be optimized (happening soon). 

The highest cross-betweenness results are exhibited by **Walerian Pańko** in 1982 and **Kazimierz Obsadny** in 1987. 

```{r}
# loading results of candidate variant #1 "Cross Betweenness"
cb_by_year <- read_csv("cb_monthly_results.csv")

cb_by_year |> arrange(desc(CrossBetweenness)) |> 
  slice_max(order_by = CrossBetweenness, n = 20) |> 
  kable(format = "html", caption = "Highest 20 Monthly Cross-Betweenness Results") |> 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = F)
```

When we compare **Jacek Kuroń** and **Lech Wałęsa** as Dr. Bodwin suggested, we see their cross-betweenness plots exhibit the predicted inversion. 

```{r fig.width= 8}
# Comparing Walesa and Kuron as suggested by Bodwin

cb_kuron_walesa <- cb_by_year |> 
  filter(Full.Name %in% c("Jacek Kuroń", "Lech Wałęsa")) |> 
    ggplot(mapping = aes(x = Start.Date,
                       y = CrossBetweenness,
                       group = Member.ID,
                       color = Full.Name)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = .75) +
  labs(title = 'Examining Cross-Betweenness in Kuroń and Wałęsa',
       x = 'Year', 
       y = 'Cross-Betweenness',
       color = '') +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),

cb_kuron_walesa
```

### Candidate Variant #2 - Cluster-Norm Cross-Betweenness

**What are we altering?**
\
We still consider the shortest paths between pairs of nodes of opposing factions, but to combat the score inflation from large organizations, we introduce a normalizing factor. 
\
We divide by the product of cluster sizes of each of the target nodes. 


**Formula:**
 $$
C_B(v) = \sum_{o \neq v \neq g}\frac{\sigma_{og}(v)}{\sigma_{og}} \cdot \frac{1}{|C_o| \cdot |C_g|}$$



Where:
\
- $\sigma_{og}$: Total number of shortest paths from node $o$, an opposition node, to node $g$, a government node.
\
- $\sigma_{og}(v)$: Number of shortest paths from node $o$ to $g$ that pass through $v$.
\
- $|C_o|$: Size of the cluster containing node $o$. 
\
- $|C_g|$: Size of the cluster containing node $g$.

**Concerns / Potential Pitfalls:**
\
We are still considering indirect interactions here, which may or may not be appropriate. 
\
While mitigating against large clusters skewing the results, we may be giving undue influence to smaller clusters. Perhaps adjusting the normalization by some factor could help. 

#### Understanding Louvain Clustering

The normalizing factor above is the product of the sizes of Louvain clusters for both the start and target nodes for each Government/Opposition pair. 

##### What is Louvain Clustering? 



```{r}
# Function to get Louvain cluster information for all RT participants
# By year

get_louvain_communities_by_year <- function(affils_by_date, on_cols,
                                            start_year = 1945,
                                            end_year   = 1989) {
  

  all_starts <- seq.Date(from = as.Date(paste0(start_year, "-01-01")),
                         to   = as.Date(paste0(end_year,   "-01-01")),
                         by   = "year")

  results <- purrr::map_dfr(all_starts, function(start_date) {
    
    end_date <- start_date %m+% years(1) - days(1)
    
    edgelist <- get_edgelist_members(
      affils_by_date,
      on_cols,
      start = start_date,
      end   = end_date
    )
    
    if(is.null(edgelist) || nrow(edgelist) == 0) {
      return(tibble(
        Member.ID         = character(0),
        LouvainCommunity  = integer(0),
        Year              = integer(0)
      ))
    }
    
    graph <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(edgelist, directed = FALSE)
    
    louvain_result <- igraph::cluster_louvain(graph)
    membership_vec <- igraph::membership(louvain_result)
    
    node_ids <- igraph::V(graph)$name
    
    tibble(
      Member.ID         = node_ids,
      LouvainCommunity  = membership_vec,
      Year              = lubridate::year(start_date)
    )
  })

  return(results)
}



```

### Comparing Spikes in CB and Cluster-Norm CB

In order to compare Cross-Betweenness and Cluster-Norm Cross-Betweenness, we need to look at instances of spikes in both scores and see if we can deduce what IAs are driving the spikes up. This will allow us to consult with Dr. Domber on which score is more useful / valid. 

Let's first take a look at Kuroń and Wałęsa. 

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2

# Plot 1
cb_kuron_walesa

# Plot 2
cncb_kuron_walesa


```

We can see that for both scores, Kuroń has a peak in 1962. This peak is not diminished with cluster-size normalization. Kuroń's smaller bumps in 1952 and 1955-1960 are driven up with the normalization. Wałęsa's spikes are almost completely flattened. Kuroń's spike in 1978 is almost flattened, as well but we still see a small bump. 

Let's see what IAs are responsible for these spikes.

## Variants of Closeness Centrality

### Standard Closeness Centrality

### Candidate Variant #3 - Cross Closeness

## Orgs-as-Nodes Metric Exploration

### PageRank in Undirected Orgs-as-Nodes 

**What is PageRank?** 
\
Variant of eigen centrality that accounts for directed edges and includes damping factor to consider probability of flow between nodes. 

**What it describes in the network?**
\
Organizations with high PageRank scores are "important" because they are connected to many other important organizations.

For example, a university that shares many members with PZPR or Solidarity will have a high PageRank.


```{r}
edgelist_orgs <- read_csv("/Users/chelseyharper/Capstone/PolandRoundTable/capstone/edgelist-orgs.csv")

```

```{r}
orgs_edges <- edgelist_orgs |> 
  filter(from != to) |> 
  arrange(desc(num_members))

# orgs_edges

g <- graph_from_data_frame(orgs_edges, directed = FALSE)

E(g)$weight <- orgs_edges$num_members
```


```{r}

page_rank_undirected <- page_rank(g, directed = FALSE,
                                  weights = E(g)$weight)

nodes_with_pagerank <- data.frame(
  Org.ID = V(g)$name,
  PageRank = page_rank_undirected$vector
)

# nodes_with_pagerank |>
#   arrange(desc(PageRank))

```

```{r}
org_meta <- read_csv('../clean_data/organization_meta_info.csv')
```
Using bidirectional graph, we can interpret the pageRank as the probability of 'passing' through a node on a random walk through the graph. 

```{r}
org_pr <- nodes_with_pagerank |> 
  inner_join(org_meta, by = 'Org.ID') 
```

```{r}

org_pr |> 
  arrange(desc(PageRank)) |> 
  slice_max(order_by = PageRank, n=10) |> 
  kable(format = "html", 
        caption = "PageRank Scores for Organizations") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = F)
  
```

### Orgs-as-Nodes Government and Opposition Comparison

```{r}
# Creating orgs nodes graph with only government affiliations

gov_g <- graph_from_data_frame(orgs_edges, directed = FALSE)
E(gov_g)$weight <- orgs_edges$Government

# Creating orgs nodes graph with only Opposition affiliations

opp_g <- graph_from_data_frame(orgs_edges, directed = FALSE)
E(opp_g)$weight <- orgs_edges$Opposition

```

```{r}
calculate_metrics <- function(g, inv_weight = FALSE) {
  if (inv_weight) {
    E(g)$weight <- 1 / E(g)$weight
  }

  metrics <- data.frame(
    Org.ID = V(g)$name,
    Degree = degree(g),
    Strength = strength(g),
    Betweenness = betweenness(g, weights = if (inv_weight) E(g)$weight else NA),
    Closeness = closeness(g, weights = if (inv_weight) E(g)$weight else NA),
    # Eigenvector = eigen_centrality(g)$vector,
    PageRank = page_rank(g, directed = FALSE, weights = E(g)$weight)$vector
  )

  return(metrics)
}


```

```{r}
#Calculate metrics for government graph
gov_metrics <- calculate_metrics(gov_g, inv_weight = TRUE)

# Calculate metrics for opposition graph
opp_metrics <- calculate_metrics(opp_g, inv_weight = TRUE)

```

## CB Results with Aggregation

```{r}
# loading results of candidate variant #1 "Cross Betweenness"
cb_by_month <- read_csv("cb_monthly_results.csv")

cb_by_month |> arrange(desc(CrossBetweenness)) |> 
  slice_max(order_by = CrossBetweenness, n = 20) |> 
  kable(format = "html", caption = "Highest 20 Monthly Cross-Betweenness Results") |> 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = F)

```

```{r}
cb_by_month <- cb_by_month |> 
  mutate(Year = format(as.Date(Start.Date), "%Y")) 

yearly_avg <- cb_by_month |> 
  group_by(Member.ID, Full.Name, RT.Affiliation, Year) |>   
  summarise(
    Yearly_Avg_CrossBetweenness = mean(CrossBetweenness, na.rm = TRUE)  
  ) |> 
  ungroup()  

overall_avg <- yearly_avg  |> 
  group_by(Member.ID, Full.Name, RT.Affiliation)  |>   
  summarise(
    Overall_Avg_CrossBetweenness = mean(Yearly_Avg_CrossBetweenness, na.rm = TRUE)  
  ) |> 
  ungroup()  

top_20_individuals <- overall_avg  |> 
  arrange(desc(Overall_Avg_CrossBetweenness)) |>  
  slice_max(order_by = Overall_Avg_CrossBetweenness, n = 20) |> 
  kable(format = "html", caption = "Highest 20 Aggregate Cross-Betweenness Results") |> 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = F)

top_20_individuals

```

```{r}
cb_agg_ziabicki <- 
  cb_by_month |> 
  filter(Full.Name %in% c("Andrzej Ziabicki")) |> 
    ggplot(mapping = aes(x = Start.Date,
                       y = CrossBetweenness,
                       group = Member.ID,
                       color = Full.Name)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = .75) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = 'Examining Aggregated Cross-Betweenness in Ziabicki',
       x = 'Year', 
       y = 'Cross-Betweenness',
       color = '') +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 12))

cb_agg_ziabicki

```



```{r}

individual_to_highlight <- "Andrzej Ziabicki"  

overall_avg <- overall_avg |> 
  mutate(Highlight = ifelse(Full.Name == individual_to_highlight, "Highlighted", "Not Highlighted"))


ggplot(overall_avg, aes(x = "", y = Overall_Avg_CrossBetweenness)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.5, fill = "steelblue", outlier.shape = NA) + 
  geom_jitter(aes(color = Highlight, alpha = Highlight), width = 0.2, size = 2) +  
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Highlighted" = "red", "Not Highlighted" = "gray")) +  
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c("Highlighted" = 1, "Not Highlighted" = 0.35), guide = "none") +  
  labs(title = paste("Distribution of Overall Average Cross-Betweenness with Highlighted Individual:", individual_to_highlight),
       x = "",
       y = "Overall Average Cross-Betweenness") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")  +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 12))


```

## We're Still Working On
- Still working on integrating CB and CNCB into the Shiny app (as a separate tab) as well as the option to see metric drivers (populate IAs) based on selected date ranges
- Still working on the table within the app that can show all individuals and allow sorting by different metrics 
- Deep dive into the Louvain clusters
  - We've started an analysis of the clusters themselves, what orgs are consigned to a single cluster / dispersed over many? What does that mean for an organization? 
   - We also want to apply Louvain to orgs-as-nodes and begin analysis there
   - We also may want to alter Louvain to redefine modularity so that cross-faction connectedness is maximized rather than overall connectedness
- Creating another metric Cross-Closeness
  - Differs from betweenness, focuses on reachability (not just shortest paths), we can define this to only look at cross-party connections
